# Isleta 2.9.1
A fix for coding agents: an island saying Claude Code needs your input could get stuck, ignoring every click and never going away.
## Fixed
- **A coding agent's island no longer gets stuck.** It leaves when the session moves on, ends, or starts a new conversation, even if the conversation was resumed in another window. - **Clicking an open coding agent's island always does something.** It goes to the agent's window when it can find one, and either way the island puts the message away and closes. - **An island you already clicked through no longer comes back.** The session shows again the next time it stops for you.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations
- **Typing your own answer still happens in the terminal.** The island offers the listed choices, and there is no going back to change an earlier one; the terminal's picker stays open until the island has answered. - **Answering from the island edits the agents' own settings.** It adds one hook to `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.codex/hooks.json`, keeps a backup, and takes exactly that back out when you turn it off. Sessions already open then keep answering in the terminal. - **Codex needs one step of its own.** Type `/hooks` in Codex once and trust Isleta's hooks. Codex waits for the island before showing its prompt, so the island lets go as soon as you're back at the terminal. - **Clicking through finds the agent's window, not its tab.** In VS Code it finds the workspace that holds the session's folder; a folder no window has open goes to VS Code's main window. A session inside tmux has no window to bring forward. - **Keeping the menus clear needs Accessibility.** Without it, the island keeps its usual width over the menu bar. A few apps change their menus without saying so; switching away and back catches up. - **The island can still cover menu bar icons beside the notch.** It keeps the menus of the app you are using clear, but macOS does not tell Isleta where other apps' icons are. - **The lean at the end of a range needs Accessibility.** Reaching the end of the volume or brightness no longer moves the island on its own, and the press after it is only visible to Isleta with that permission granted. The reading itself, and the bar filling and emptying, work either way. - **A muted Mac's bar cannot be dragged.** It is drawn at nothing whatever the volume behind it is, so pressing it opens the island instead. Unmute first. - **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. Isleta shows that a call is happening and nothing more. - **Weather needs your location, or a city you type.** Isleta asks for neither until you use it. - **A connected device's battery is read once, when it connects.** It does not tick down as you wear them, and most non-Apple headphones report no level at all. - **A timer started by Siri, Shortcuts or Control Center can take a few seconds to appear.** One started by hand in Clock is there immediately. - **Replacing the system HUDs is on by default, and it needs Accessibility.** Two switches in Settings hand the keys back. Quitting Isleta hands them back too; if Isleta is force-quit, the system HUD stays out of the way until Isleta next starts. Brightness covers the built-in display only. - **Apple's own banner still appears when headphones connect.** It is drawn by the menu bar rather than by the HUD helper Isleta can stand in for, so the island announces the connection alongside it rather than instead of it. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a floating island can sit over the middle of the space labels. - **Today and tomorrow show five entries and then a count.** A busy pair of days says how many it could not fit rather than scrolling. - **The equalizer moves in a set pattern rather than to the song.** Its colors come from the cover; its motion does not come from the audio.

# Isleta 2.9.0
When Claude Code asks you a question, you can answer it from the island: its choices appear as buttons, one question at a time.
## New
- **Answer Claude Code's questions from the island.** With "Answer prompts from the island" on in Settings ▸ Sources, pick an option and the next question follows; where several answers are allowed, tick them and press Submit. Claude carries on as if you had chosen in the terminal.
- **Isleta speaks Japanese.** The island, Settings and the first-run window follow your Mac when it is set to Japanese.
## Improved
- **The island says where the agent is working.** Under the headline it names the project's folder, such as "Sites/my-app", instead of the session's own name.
## Fixed
- **A question is no longer offered as Allow or Deny.** Neither button answered it; the island now shows the question itself, or leaves it to the terminal.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac without one gets a floating island on the main display.
## Known limitations

Sessions already open then keep answering in the terminal. - **Codex needs one step of its own.** Type `/hooks` in Codex once and trust Isleta's hooks. Codex waits for the island before showing its prompt, so the island lets go as soon as you're back at the terminal. - **Clicking through finds the agent's window, not its tab.** In VS Code it finds the workspace that holds the session's folder; a folder no window has open goes to VS Code's main window. A session inside tmux has no window to bring forward. - **Keeping the menus clear needs Accessibility.** Without it, the island keeps its usual width over the menu bar. A few apps change their menus without saying so; switching away and back catches up. - **The island can still cover menu bar icons beside the notch.** It keeps the menus of the app you are using clear, but macOS does not tell Isleta where other apps' icons are. - **The lean at the end of a range needs Accessibility.** Reaching the end of the volume or brightness no longer moves the island on its own, and the press after it is only visible to Isleta with that permission granted. The reading itself, and the bar filling and emptying, work either way. - **A muted Mac's bar cannot be dragged.** It is drawn at nothing whatever the volume behind it is, so pressing it opens the island instead. Unmute first. - **You cannot see who is calling.** macOS does not let apps outside Apple read that, or answer for you. # Isleta 2.8.0
The island tells you when Claude Code or Codex needs you, and can answer its permission prompts for you: Allow or Deny, right from the notch.
## New
- **Claude Code and Codex in the island.** When an agent stops for you or finishes while you're in another app, your terminal's icon appears with a raised hand, and the agent's mark beside it. - **Click to see what it needs, and again to go there.** The open island says whether it wants permission or an answer, in which session, and a second click brings its window forward on whichever desktop it's on. - **Allow or Deny from the island.** Turn on "Answer permission prompts from the island" in Settings ▸ Sources and the island shows the command being asked about, with buttons under it. Allow approves that one request and changes none of your rules.
## Improved
- **Volume, charging and devices show through a crowded menu bar.** When an app's menus need the room beside the notch, the island still announces a key press, the charger or AirPods connecting, then gets out of the way again.
